message.content:
Hello! I'm excited to share some feedback on your recent lesson. Your overall score is 68%, with 19 out of 28 marks. 

One major strength in your lesson was the use of concrete models and real-world connections. You effectively used examples like a cake to make the concept of fractions more relatable for the students. This approach helped students move from just identifying shapes to using important vocabulary and explaining their thinking. 

A key growth opportunity is in the area of feedback. While you provided plenty of prompts, you could enhance student learning by offering specific feedback. For instance, after a student identifies the numerator, you could say, "Great job! Now, can you tell me why that is the numerator?" This will encourage deeper understanding and engagement.

Keep up the great work! Your commitment to improving student learning is evident, and with a few tweaks, you'll make even more impact. Keep encouraging those quieter students, and see how it transforms their participation. You're doing a fantastic job!
